text: A request may be routed to a registered tool when the tool purpose matches the user's intent.
An agent can decompose a complex request, while a skill can provide a focused capability.
A direct greeting is normally a no-call decision unless a capability is explicitly requested.
A missing required input can make a valid capability request require clarification.
An unsupported request should not produce a fabricated capability identifier.
The active registry is an immutable snapshot for one routing request.
A changed capability description requires a fresh description embedding.
A tokenizer preserves Unicode by encoding text as strict UTF-8 bytes.
Literal structural token spellings in content remain ordinary bytes.
The request formatter removes the oldest complete history entry when context is full.
The current user request is never silently truncated.
Retrieval scores registered descriptions using normalized dot product.
The operational shortlist contains at most eight capabilities.
A clear retrieval margin may skip cross-encoding and use the fast path.
An ambiguous shortlist is reranked before the decision classifier runs.
Reranker scores are relevance scores, not confidence probabilities.
The decision classifier returns CALL, NO_CALL, or CLARIFY.
The classifier cannot select a capability outside the final ranked candidates.
A no-call result carries a null capability identifier.
An empty registry returns NO_CALL after request validation.
Exact score ties use ascending ASCII capability identifiers.
Padding rows are zeroed after every residual branch.
Layer normalization statistics are evaluated in float32.
Attention is bidirectional and does not use a causal mask.
RoPE rotates adjacent query and key coordinate pairs.
The retrieval head pools ordinary content positions and excludes structural tokens.
A candidate artifact records its source, checkpoint, tokenizer, and calibration identities.
A safe tensor checkpoint preserves optimizer and random-state information for resume.
An INT8 artifact must retain floating point task heads unless separately validated.
Benchmark failures and unsupported backends remain visible in the result matrix.
A reviewer audits an exact candidate source commit independently.
The encoder selects a receiver; it does not execute the receiver's action.
